question: Is r49's weak monsoon peak (Mexico Jul-Aug ~1/4 of observed, Sahel and Texas low) a grid-resolution effect or missing physics?
runs: r49 (calibration/local_accuracy_20261023/r49_params.json) unchanged, scripts/benchmark_local.py at --cell-km 56 (existing r49 adoption runs), 28 and 14 on mexico, texas_plains (dev12 specs), sahel_niger (retired_b specs); bengal and najd_arabia as guards (retired_b)
measure: peak ratio = region-mean simulated rain / observed rain over the region's three wettest observed months (cells from the run's cells/*.npz); also the annual ratio
rule: RESOLUTION if the 14 km peak ratio exceeds the 56 km one by >= 0.25 (absolute) in at least 2 of the 3 target regions -> the finer grid is the lever (report; no physics change). Otherwise PHYSICS -> proceed to the declared physics step (two-level moisture transport, then land-sea inflow), each screened on dev and tested once on sealed set o.
no_scoring: diagnostic only; no parameter is fitted and no sealed set is opened
